title: Find connections without inventing history
goal: Distinguish an analogy, a documented influence and a factual relationship.
explanation: An unexpected connection is an idea to investigate, not evidence that one system caused another. Separate analogy from history and verify specific claims independently. The Roman Empire and cloud computing can invite useful comparisons, but modern technical terms should not be projected backward as literal ancient systems.
sampleInput: Compare a Roman road network with a modern distributed computing network. Possible dimensions: routes, hubs, disruption, maintenance and administration. No historical document or technical specification is supplied.
prompt: Suggest three clearly labelled ANALOGIES between these systems. For each, explain one useful comparison and one important difference. Put historical or technical factual claims in a separate verification-needed list. Do not invent direct influence, quotations or ancient equivalents of digital technology.
workedExample: Analogy: both can involve alternative routes around disruption. Difference: roads transport physical travellers/goods; computer networks move encoded information under protocols. “Romans invented cloud load balancing” is not an acceptable factual conclusion.

steps.title: Name relationship types
steps.text: Define analogy, factual claim and causal influence before querying.

steps.title: Generate three candidates
steps.text: Ask for useful similarities plus differences, not a sensational hidden-history narrative.

steps.title: Tag each sentence
steps.text: Mark it analogy, factual assertion or unsupported causal claim.

steps.title: Verify one assertion
steps.text: Consult an authoritative historical or technical source and record the exact supporting passage.

steps.title: Build a cautious map
steps.text: Use solid edges for verified relationships and dashed edges for analogies or hypotheses.

checks: Each connection is labelled by type and includes an explicit difference.
At least one factual assertion has independently checked evidence or remains unresolved.
No analogy is reported as proof of historical influence.
commonMistakes: Mistaking a clever parallel for causation.
Inventing citations to make a surprising story sound credible.
offline: Compare two familiar systems on paper and label the analogy boundaries without making historical claims.
reflection: Which connection stayed useful after you removed its exaggerated historical claim?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Each connection is labelled by type and includes an explicit difference.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. At least one factual assertion has independently checked evidence or remains unresolved.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Mistaking a clever parallel for causation.
